I am 58 years old, and I have been farming these lands in Quzhou since I was a young man. My family has about 10 mu of good flat land on the North China Plain. I finished middle school, which was enough to read seed labels and fertilizer instructions, and over the decades I have learned what works here. The soil is loamy, the groundwater is reachable, and the machinery cooperative helps with planting and harvest. I do not chase risky new crops — I leave that to the younger entrepreneurs with greenhouses. My priority is stable grain income to feed my family and have something left to sell.

This year, I will stick to the wheat–maize double-cropping system that has always fed us. All 10 mu will go into winter wheat starting this autumn, and after the June harvest I will immediately plant summer maize on the same 10 mu. I might lose sleep during the rush between harvest and sowing, but the returns are reliable. For wheat, I will buy an improved variety like Shimai 22 or Liangxing 77 from the county supply shop — the seeds are clean and the yield is steady around 1,000 jin per mu. Before sowing I will rotary-till the field to break up the maize stubble and level the ground. I will spread about 100 jin of compound fertilizer as basal dressing and follow with one topdressing of urea at green-up. Water is precious, so I will irrigate three times: once at overwintering, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. I also spray herbicide once and insecticide twice to keep aphids and diseases away.

For the summer maize, I will plant a hybrid variety such as Nongda 372. Time is short after wheat harvest, so I will use no-tillage direct seeding — the cooperative drill can plant straight into the wheat stubble. Maize needs less fertilizer than wheat because the wheat residue and leftover nutrients help, so I will put down roughly 80 jin of compound fertilizer at sowing and maybe a side-dressing of urea at the big-flare stage if the leaves look yellow. Two irrigations are usually enough: one at jointing and one at filling. I will spray herbicide once and insecticide twice for corn borers. I expect about 1,100 jin per mu from the maize, and with current prices that should cover my costs and give me a modest profit.
